header.name: Econometrics with machine learning
header.description: This course covers applications of high-dimensional statistics and machine learning to econometrics, including variable selection, inference with high-dimensional nuisance parameters, heterogeneity, treatment allocation, networks and 'textual' data. The focus will be on policy evaluation problems using large economic and social datasets. Specifically, we will answer following questions: 1) What are the similarities between econometric and machine learning techniques? 2) To what extent can machine learning techniques assist econometric investigation of human behavior? 3) Can machine learning techniques assist in testing statistical hypotheses and identifying causal relationships in ‘big data'? 4) How can existing econometric techniques be extended by incorporating machine learning concepts?

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Compare and contrast different econometric and machine learning methods to analyse economic and social data.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Implement machine learning methods in econometric analyses.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Asymptotic properties and interpretation in ecnometric models that are enhanced with machine learning methods.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Formulate a research question and analyze it with real-world data using models in econometrics and machine learning methods

lecture_topics: A contrast (differences and similarities) between econometric methods and machine learning techniques
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: A short project will be assigned based on a real-world dataset. At the end of the semester, students will present their findings/contributions.
